reader.requirement: With WITH NO ADVANCING the device position is left immediately after the last character of the last operand displayed, with no line reset.

edition-consulted.switches: refuses END-DISPLAY and a numeric DISPLAY literal that is not an unsigned integer below 2002 (SR2 and a later form, not the transfer)
the national and boolean literal rows that refuse N".." and B".." operands at 85 (operand class, not the transfer)

reader.edition-search: grep of AcceptDisplayEmitter.cs, AcceptDisplayBinder.cs and OperandText.cs for Edition, DialectLevel, DialectBehavior, CobolVersion: the transfer (BoundDisplay to Console.Write or WriteLine of the concatenated device strings) consults no edition; the numeric device form is the --numeric-display option (EditionContext.NumericDisplay, default Decimal), not an edition switch. The only edition sites on the DISPLAY path are compile-time refusals of later forms.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no: the transfer is the same code at every edition; only the admitted operand forms (signed numeric literal, national and boolean literals, END-DISPLAY) differ
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witness covers the default device; UPON a mnemonic-name, multiple operands and a last DISPLAY of the run are not exercised

reader.notes: BoundDisplay.NoAdvancing selects Console.Write instead of WriteLine, for the default device and for UPON (U1U2 on one line); the run's last DISPLAY WITH NO ADVANCING leaves no trailing newline (od shows LAST at end of file).
